This is an email I sent earlier today to all employees at Coinbase:

Team,

Today I’ve made the difficult decision to reduce the size of Coinbase by ~14%. I want to walk you through why we're doing this now, what it means for those affected, and how this positions us for the future.

Why now
Two forces are converging at the same time. We need to be front footed to respond to both.

First, the market. Coinbase is well-capitalized, has diversified revenue streams, and is well-positioned to weather any storm. Crypto is also on the verge of the next wave of adoption, with stablecoins, prediction markets, tokenization, and more taking off. However, our business is still volatile from quarter to quarter. While we've managed through that cyclicality many times before and come out stronger on the other side, we’re currently in a down market and need to adjust our cost structure now so that we emerge from this period leaner, faster, and more efficient for our next phase of growth.

Second, AI is changing how we work. Over the past year, I’ve watched engineers use AI to ship in days what used to take a team weeks. Non-technical teams are now shipping production code and many of our workflows are being automated. The pace of what's possible with a small, focused team has changed dramatically, and it's accelerating every day.

All of this has led us to an inflection point, not just for Coinbase, but for every company. The biggest risk now is not taking action. We are adjusting early and deliberately to rebuild Coinbase to be lean, fast, and AI-native. We need to return to the speed and focus of our startup founding, with AI at our core.

What this means
To get there, we are not just reducing headcount and cutting costs, we’re fundamentally changing how we operate: rebuilding Coinbase as an intelligence, with humans around the edge aligning it. What does this mean in practice?

- Fewer layers, faster decisions: We are flattening our org structure to 5 layers max below CEO/COO. Layers slow things down and create coordination tax. The future is small, high context teams that can move quickly. Leaders will own much more, with as many as 15+ direct reports. Fewer layers also means a leaner cost structure that is built to perform through all market cycles.

- No pure managers: Every leader at Coinbase must also be a strong and active individual contributor. Managers should be like player-coaches, getting their hands dirty alongside their teams.

- AI-native pods: We’ll be concentrating around AI-native talent who can manage fleets of agents to drive outsized impact. We’ll also be experimenting with reduced pod sizes, including “one person teams” with engineers, designers, and product managers all in one role.

In short: AI is bringing a profound shift in how companies operate, and we’re reshaping Coinbase to lead in this new era. This is a new way of working, and we need to leverage AI across every facet of our jobs.

To those who are affected
I know there are real people behind these decisions — talented colleagues who have poured themselves into this company and our mission. To those of you who will be leaving: thank you. You’ve helped build Coinbase into what it is today, and I am sincerely grateful for everything you've done.

All impacted team members will receive an email to their personal account in the next hour with more information, and an invitation to meet with an HRBP and a senior leader in your organization. Coinbase system access has been removed today. I know this feels sudden and harsh, but it is the only responsible choice given our duty to protect customer information.

To those affected, we will be providing a comprehensive package to support you through this transition. US employees will receive a minimum of 16 weeks base pay (plus 2 weeks per year worked), their next equity vest, and 6 months of COBRA. Employees on a work visa will get extra transition support. Those outside of the US will receive similar support, based on local factors and subject to any consultation requirements.

Coinbase prides itself on talent density. Our employees are among the most talented people in the world, and I have no doubt that your skills and experience will be highly sought after as you pursue your next chapters.

How we move forward
To the team that is staying, I know this is a difficult day. We’re saying goodbye to colleagues and friends you've been in the trenches with. But here’s what I want you to know as we move forward together:

Over the past 13 years, we have weathered four crypto winters, gone public, and built the most trusted platform in our industry. We’ve made it this far by making hard decisions and by always staying focused on our mission. This time will be no different – nothing has changed about the long term outlook of our company or industry. And most importantly, our mission has never been more important for the world. Increasing economic freedom requires a new financial system, and we’re building it.

The Coinbase that emerges from this will be more capable than ever to achieve our mission.

Brian

recent_posts.title: agents need control flow, not more prompts
recent_posts.summary: Reliable AI agents require deterministic control flow encoded in software rather than elaborate prompt chains. Prompts are non-deterministic, weakly specified, and don't compose reliably as complexity grows. The argument is that LLMs should be treated as components within a deterministic scaffold with explicit state transitions and validation checkpoints. Without programmatic verification, teams are left choosing between keeping a human in the loop, exhaustive post-run auditing, or blindly accepting outputs.

recent_posts.title: GitHub - wojtczyk/trust: TRUST – Coding Rust like it's 1989
recent_posts.summary: TRUST is an experimental retro TUI IDE for Rust projects that mimics classic blue-screen DOS development environments. It supports file editing, project browsing, and running Cargo commands (build, run, test, check) via keyboard shortcuts and menus. The project is self-hosting — TRUST can build TRUST — and supports mouse interaction, pane resizing, and clipboard operations.

recent_posts.title: GitHub - antirez/ds4: DeepSeek 4 Flash local inference engine for Metal
recent_posts.summary: ds4.c is a narrow, Metal-only local inference engine specifically built for DeepSeek V4 Flash, a 284B MoE model. It is not a generic GGUF runner but a purpose-built engine with DS4-specific loading, KV state management, and an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible HTTP server API. Key features include: 2-bit quantization that runs on MacBooks with 128GB RAM, a disk-based KV cache that persists session state across restarts, a 1M token context window, and integration with coding agents like Claude Code, opencode, and Pi. The disk KV cache design treats SSD storage as a first-class citizen for KV state, enabling long-context inference without keeping everything in RAM. Performance benchmarks show 26 t/s generation on an M3 Max MacBook Pro and 36 t/s on an M3 Ultra Mac Studio. The project was built with significant GPT-4.5 assistance and is explicitly alpha-quality, Metal-only (CPU path crashes macOS due to a VM bug), and only works with the custom GGUF files published by the author.

recent_posts.title: AlphaEvolve: Gemini-powered coding agent scaling impact across fields
recent_posts.summary: AlphaEvolve, Google DeepMind's Gemini-powered coding agent, has moved from pilot to production use across Google's infrastructure and commercial partners. It has optimized next-generation TPU circuit designs, improved Google Spanner's LSM-tree compaction by reducing write amplification 20%, and cut software storage footprint by 9%. Commercial deployments include Klarna doubling transformer training speed, FM Logistic achieving 10.4% routing efficiency gains, Schrödinger getting 4x speedup in ML force field training, and WPP gaining 10% accuracy in campaign models. AlphaEvolve is now available to external enterprises via Google Cloud.

recent_posts.title: RaTeX — Rust math layout aligned with KaTeX golden tests
recent_posts.summary: RaTeX is a Rust-based TeX-style math layout engine that parses LaTeX math and emits a flat display list for rendering on CoreGraphics, Skia, Canvas 2D, or custom backends. It targets native apps (iOS, Android, Flutter) and servers where a WebView or JavaScript runtime is undesirable. The engine is validated against KaTeX golden test suites with pixel-diff CI. Ready-to-use packages are available for Web (WASM via npm), Android (Maven), Flutter (pub.dev), and iOS (SPM). Compared to KaTeX and MathJax, RaTeX uses pure Rust with no GC in the hot path, zero JS bundle size, and predictable memory behavior. It also supports mhchem-style chemistry macros (\ce, \pu) out of the box, which competing native SDKs like swiftMath, flutter_math, and iosMath lack.

recent_posts.title: Motherboard market shrinks 28% as AI chip demand squeezes consumer PC components
recent_posts.summary: Motherboard sales are collapsing in 2026, with the four major manufacturers — Asus, Gigabyte, MSI, and ASRock — collectively facing a ~28% market contraction. The primary driver is AI infrastructure demand pulling chipmakers like Nvidia, Intel, and AMD away from consumer chip production, causing shortages and price increases across memory, storage, and CPUs. Asus is projected to sell 33% fewer boards year-on-year, while ASRock faces the steepest drop at 37%. The lack of compelling new CPU socket transitions and no Nvidia RTX 50 Super refresh are further discouraging upgrades. Some manufacturers are offsetting losses by pivoting to AI server production.

recent_posts.title: How to Make LLM Training Faster with Unsloth and NVIDIA
recent_posts.summary: Unsloth collaborated with NVIDIA to achieve ~25% faster LLM training through three targeted optimizations. First, packed-sequence metadata caching eliminates repeated reconstruction of attention masks and sequence metadata across transformer layers, yielding up to +43.3% forward pass speedup on Qwen3-14B QLoRA SFT. Second, double-buffered activation checkpoint reloading overlaps CPU-to-GPU memory copies with backward compute, delivering 4.6–8.4% step-time improvements on 8B–32B dense models with minimal VRAM overhead. Third, MoE routing is improved by replacing per-expert dynamic torch.where queries with a single bincount pass, reducing CPU-GPU synchronization overhead proportional to num_experts down to a constant, yielding 10–15% speedups on GPT-OSS configurations. All three optimizations target overhead in the 'glue code' around main kernels rather than the kernels themselves, and are automatically enabled on RTX laptops, data center GPUs, and DGX Spark machines after updating Unsloth.

recent_posts.title: TI-83 Plus BASIC Programming Tutorial: A Beginners' Guide
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive beginner's guide to programming the TI-83 Plus calculator using TI-BASIC. Covers core output functions (DISP, OUTPUT, CLRHOME), control flow (LBL/GOTO, FOR, WHILE, IF/THEN/ELSE), user input (INPUT, PROMPT, GETKEY), variables, strings, lists, matrices, random number generation, and drawing functions (LINE, CIRCLE, SHADE, Pt-On/Pt-Off). Includes code examples, comparisons between loop types, and programming challenges to practice skills.

recent_posts.title: Photoshop’s challenges with focus, pt. 2 – Unsung
recent_posts.summary: A detailed critique of Photoshop 2026's 'modern user interface' (Spectrum) redesign, focusing on numerous focus-handling regressions. Issues documented include: first field not auto-focused on dialog open, values not pre-selected on click, hover states not matching focus behavior, backspacing triggering error modals that steal focus, tab order including irrelevant controls, and checkboxes not restoring focus to last control. The author argues these are solved problems in UI engineering, representing carelessness and a failure of imagination rather than technical difficulty. Suggestions for improvement include lighter error feedback, equation support in fields, and better keyboard shortcut discoverability.

recent_posts.title: [2605.03546] ProgramBench: Can Language Models Rebuild Programs From Scratch?
recent_posts.summary: ProgramBench is a new benchmark evaluating whether LLM-based software engineering agents can rebuild entire programs from scratch given only a reference executable and its documentation. Unlike existing benchmarks that focus on narrow tasks like bug fixes or single features, ProgramBench requires agents to make holistic software architecture decisions. The 200 tasks span compact CLI tools to major projects like FFmpeg, SQLite, and the PHP interpreter. Behavioral tests are generated via agent-driven fuzzing without prescribing implementation structure. Evaluating 9 language models, none fully resolved any task — the best model passed 95% of tests on only 3% of tasks. A notable finding is that models tend to produce monolithic single-file implementations that diverge significantly from human-written code.
